question: Which markers are measured before and after orchidectomy?
explanation: AFP, β-hCG, and LDH should be determined before and after orchidectomy and throughout follow-up [1].
sourceArticle: EAU Guidelines on Testicular Cancer, limited update April 2024

question: Stage IS means:

options.A: After orchidectomy the markers rise, stay elevated, or do not fall as their half-lives predict
options.B: A normal marker and a normal CT
options.C: Pure seminoma confined to the testis

correctAnswerText: After orchidectomy the markers rise, stay elevated, or do not fall as their half-lives predict
explanation: Stage IS is persistent or rising markers, or failure to decline as expected by half-lives, after orchidectomy, implying subclinical metastatic disease [1].
sourceArticle: EAU Guidelines on Testicular Cancer, limited update April 2024

question: When is one course of BEP a strong recommendation in stage I non-seminoma?

options.A: When the patient will not undergo or comply with surveillance
options.B: For every patient instead of surveillance
options.C: Only after relapse in the brain
options.E: As the treatment of a contralateral benign cyst

correctAnswerText: When the patient will not undergo or comply with surveillance
explanation: One course of cisplatin, etoposide, and bleomycin is an adjuvant alternative, with a strong recommendation, if the patient is not willing to undergo or comply with surveillance [1].
sourceArticle: EAU Guidelines on Testicular Cancer, limited update April 2024

question: Median sensitivity and specificity of abdominal contrast CT for staging are:
explanation: For abdominal staging, contrast CT has a median sensitivity of 67% and specificity of 95% [1].
sourceArticle: EAU Guidelines on Testicular Cancer, limited update April 2024

question: Why can the diagnosis be delayed?

options.A: Pain, whether scrotal or in the abdomen or back, may be present and delay recognition of a usually painless mass
options.D: The mass is always painful, so delay is impossible

correctAnswerText: Pain, whether scrotal or in the abdomen or back, may be present and delay recognition of a usually painless mass
explanation: Presentation is often a painless mass or an incidental ultrasound finding. Scrotal or abdominal or back pain may occur and can delay diagnosis [1].
sourceArticle: EAU Guidelines on Testicular Cancer, limited update April 2024
